title: Pager oscillation and threshold stability notes
content:
TL;DR: Over the last 3 months we've seen recurring pager oscillation where an SLO burn alert flips on/off repeatedly (often coupling to transient missing metrics and ingestion latency). This doc captures observed patterns, quick mitigations, proposed runbook edits, and concrete queries/dashboard changes to reduce noise while preserving SLO visibility.

Context / why I wrote this
- Several noisy incidents in Nov–Dec 2024 where oncall pagers fired repeatedly (sometimes 4–5 times in 2 hours) for the same customer-facing SLO.
- Symptoms: alert fires, then resolves when metric is backfilled or sampler recovers, then fires again. Sometimes coincides with downstream exporter GC spikes or collector restarts.
- Impact: Pager fatigue -> escalations -> chasing symptom not cause. We need stability in alert decisioning and clearer separation of missing-data vs true burn.

Recent incidents (summary)
- 2024-11-12 03:10 UTC: slo_high_latency_burn (90m window) fired briefly, resolved in ~7m. Root cause: Fluent-exporter restart on a node pool rolling update. Metric gap in requests.latency_95 spiked.
- 2024-12-03 18:45 UTC: slo_error_rate_burn flapped 3x over 90m. Deeper: distributed aggregator went into backpressure -> partial write failures -> metrics low-sample then spike.
- 2024-12-22 09:02 UTC: synthetic-latency probe failed concurrently with a collector OOM; alert resolved when OOM pod restarted and metrics replayed.

Observed patterns (hypotheses)
1) Missing/late metrics masquerading as SLO burn. Our current SLO alerts do not distinguish low-sample or stale-series from genuine increased error/latency.
2) Alert decision window too sensitive to short-lived blips: 15–30m evaluation windows + immediate paging cause noise.
3) Aggregation buckets with small n are noisy when telemetry drops (customer-specific routes with low RPS).
4) Downstream relays/extractors are single points for many metric series — when they hiccup, many related alerts trigger simultaneously (alert storms).

Evidence & reproducible queries
- Quick check for series freshness (PromQL):
  max_over_time((time() - timestamp(requests_latency_95{job="exporter"}))[30m:])
  -> flags series with last value older than 5m.
- Count of missing series for a tenant (BigQuery pseudo):
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS series_missing FROM telemetry.series_meta WHERE last_seen_ts < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY series_missing DESC;
- Example: rolling_flap pattern: (PromQL)
  increase(alert_notifications_total{alertname="slo_error_rate_burn",region!="test"}[1h]) > 3
  -> quick way to surface oscillating alerts per region.

Immediate mitigations (what oncall should do during a flare)
1) Check series freshness before action: run the freshness query for the alert's principal metrics. If series are stale, add note "probable metric ingestion gap" and escalate to observability infra team instead of paging product owners.
2) If multiple related SLOs are firing, suspect upstream exporter/collector; check k8s events for recent restarts (kubectl get events -n observability).
3) Use grouping and silence as short-term: if the same alert repeats within 10 minutes and we see "series not fresh" evidence, create a 30m silence for the alert with comment "metric ingestion suspected".
4) For true SLO degradation (fresh series + sustained burn > 20m), follow full incident runbook.

Runbook edits proposed (concrete)
- Add step 0.5 (pre-runbook): verify-series-freshness. Add code snippet for PromQL/BQ used above.
- Split `slo_*_burn` into two alert layers:
  * slo_burn_signal: no paging; fires to dashboard and a low-severity channel for detection ops (evaluation window = 10m, but no phone).
  * slo_burn_page: paging rule that requires both (a) burn signal and (b) metric freshness confirmed or corroborating traffic/op traces. Evaluation window for page: 30m aggregated.
- Debounce policy: require at least two consecutive evaluations to be true before page (reduces single-blip pages).
- Add metric-presence alert (warning) that groups by exporter/collector: if > X series from the same exporter are stale, page infra team. This isolates collector-level failures.

Suggested alert parameter changes (concrete numbers to test)
- Current: slo_burn page window = 15m, immediate page.
- Proposal A (conservative): page window -> 30m; require freshness check; add 10m cooldown per unique alert instance.
- Proposal B (for low-volume routes): use relative-sample thresholds: if series sample count < 50 samples in 1h, change burn alerts to warning-only and require synthetic checks to confirm.

Dashboard / UX changes (quick wins)
- Add a "freshness" row on the SLO dashboard: show percent of series with last_seen < 5m over the last 30m.
- Dashboard should display exporter pod names and last_restart_time next to top-N flaky series.
- Add a compact "oscillation history" panel: timeseries of alert state transitions for last 24h (helps triage flaky alerts quickly).

Acceptance criteria for changes
- Reduce pages from these SLO alerts by >50% over a 30d window without increasing undetected SLO degradation incidents.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) not worsening for legitimate pages.
- No customer-visible SLA violations due to delayed pages (we'll monitor closely for 4 weeks after change).

Implementation plan and rollouts
1) Week 0: deploy metric-presence alert to staging and replicate a missing-series scenario to validate no false pages. Owner: Priya.
2) Week 1: implement freshness check helper in alerting rules; run in shadow mode (no page) for production for 7 days. Owner: Diego.
3) Week 2: enable two-tier rule (slo_burn_signal + slo_burn_page) with conservative windows; keep short silences possible from oncall. Owner: Maya.
4) Week 4: collect metrics, run buyback analysis (pages vs real incidents), then tweak windows. Owner: SRE leads.

Measuring success (what to track)
- alert_fire_count per alert / day (compare before/after).
- unique_pager_targets_hit per alert.
- correlation_rate of alert fires to metric freshness=false (we want this to drop).
- SLO analytic: percent of true SLO violations that were detected and paged within target window.

Open questions / risks
- Risk: increasing evaluation windows may delay real incident pages for short but real regressions. Mitigation: keep lower-severity signal channel for quick eyes and synthetic probes.
- Q: What is the right freshness threshold for all tenants? 2m vs 5m vs 10m tradeoffs need testing.
- Q: For low-volume routes, when is variance legitimately high? We should flag these and treat differently.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Priya: spin up metric-presence alert in staging + test harness (due 2024-11-15).
- Diego: add freshness helper and shadow in prod for 7d (start 2024-11-18).
- Maya: prototype dashboard panels + osc history (due 2024-11-25).
- Liam: review two-tier paging rule and sign off (due 2024-12-02).
- Ruth: create playbook PR with new runbook steps (due 2024-12-04).

Notes to self / informal thoughts
- We should avoid a heavyweight one-size-fits-all: alerts that make sense for high-RPS system A will be noise for low-RPS system B. Consider templated alert profiles per tenant class.
- Consider adding a small ML-based clustering that groups alerts by upstream exporter/pod restart event — will help auto-silence and route to infra automatically. Low priority.
- Make sure Confluence doc (linked) has a clear "how to decide to silence" rubric so rotating oncall knows what to do.

Evidence attachments / graphs to include before PR
- 11/12 incident graph: requests.latency_95 (series drop) + exporter restarts timeline.
- 12/03 incident: aggregated alerts spike heatmap.
- Synthetic probe vs production metric timeline (show mismatch).

Postmortem template additions (for next PMs)
- Add a dedicated section: "Was this caused by metric loss?" with checklist (freshness: yes/no, exporter restarts: yes/no, backlog/backpressure: yes/no).
- If metric loss = yes, then recommend: silence pager for 30m and page infra with collector-specific alert.

References / related
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-772: "Metric freshness playbook" (draft)
- JIRA-SRE-331: "Reduce noise from slo_burn alerts"
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/789 (freshness helper)

Quick wins to implement right away
- Add helper to template alerts that references series freshness as a required condition for paging.
- Surface exporter last_restart_time on SLO dashboards.
- Batch related alerts by exporter instance (join labels).

If you want to push on one thing first: implement the shadow freshness check in prod so we can quantify how many pages would have been suppressed. That gives us data to justify longer evaluation windows and debouncing.

-- Maya (notes during oncall reviews, initial draft).

Unresolved: pick final numbers for windows (30m vs 45m), sample thresholds for low-volume routes. Let's discuss in next SRE sync (agenda item).
